title: The Ice Villager Joins the Fight
synopsis: Movie 5 opens with an announcer segment: Basil has left the Super Family, and Kopeka, an ice villager, is the newest recruit. The family gathers at Mata Nui, trades morning-routine banter, and worries after the Toa never returned from a scouting mission against the Bohrok. Sensing an "ultimate evil," the team rallies together, pooling their power into one final blast, and marches off to confront Makuta's lair.

title: Makuta's Obedient Form
synopsis: The heroes face down one of Makuta's "obedient forms" in a rapid-fire toy battle, trading elemental attacks, a shielding "block screen," and a climactic hyper beam. Between hits the kids narrate combo attacks and taunts until the enemy is finally declared knocked out, but Makuta vows there's more fighting to come.

title: Chrono Shields and Cheap Shots
synopsis: More back-and-forth trash talk with Makuta, who's accused of "getting bored" and hiding behind "chrono shielding," while new fighters Sheila and Agent Nine jump into the fray with blasters. The narration is heavy on taunts and repeated lines as the toy battle grinds on, action escalating into a climbing, chaotic scramble.

title: Crystal Beam Confusion
synopsis: The battle intensifies as the heroes deploy a crystal beam and a "super confusion" attack to try to knock out their foe, while enemies fire their most powerful blasts skyward in a repeated, over-the-top barrage. It ends on a twist: the villains claim to have defeated the whole Super Family, except for Dr. Senor and Stacey.

title: Earning Your Kanohi
synopsis: After a rough surgery scare, the heroes take a breather to meditate and dodge Makuta's confusion attack, trading jabs about who's actually "earned" their Kanohi mask yet. The action shifts to the Tohunga warriors joining the fray, masks flipping on and off as everyone gears up to battle the spirit of Makuta together.

title: The Invisible Crab and the Weather Witch
synopsis: A short, scrappy round of skirmishing sees one of the heroes deploy a mysterious "invisible crab" attack while the team debates whether it counts as their most powerful move. The water-elemental fighter, apparently tempted toward the evil side, is eventually blasted down and taken on by Stacy, who's warned that their foe can control the weather.

title: Makuta's Sons
synopsis: The battle rolls into an extended showdown where Makuta rallies with a grand speech about his eternal duty to "protect the universe," then bitterly reveals that his own sons have been destroyed in the fighting, naming them one by one. It ends with Makuta powering up through a mysterious "Powerball" for one last attack, which the heroes vow to block.

title: The Last Battle and a Tape from the Past
synopsis: Makuta falls for good, the Super Family celebrates, and the young director signs off, promising the next movie will be a battle-free Christmas special. But the tape doesn't stop rolling: it rolls into leftover footage from an old recorded broadcast, an unrelated Redwall TV segment about a warlord called Clooney the Scourge, heraldry, and a trivia quiz, accidentally preserved on the same tape.

title: Countdown to Christmas Begins
synopsis: The Super Family kicks off its battle-free Christmas special with everyday morning routines: breakfast, mask painting, and Stacy getting help with her Chinese homework from Nakama. Between gift-planning chatter and a parade of babies needing baths and snacks, the household settles into cozy holiday-prep mode.

title: Pineapple Pie and Days-Before-Christmas Math
synopsis: The family gathers for a chaotic holiday dinner, complete with a rambling bedtime-style story about a skyscraper family, a spread of pineapple pie and "cookie delight," and a running joke about exactly how many days before Christmas it actually is. Kids clamor for food while the parents wrangle plates, babies, and a growing crowd around the table.

title: Bath Time and Feather Duty
synopsis: It's bath night for the littlest Super Family members, with shampoo-versus-soap mixups and careful feather- and wing-brushing for the winged babies, plus a whirlpool tub that gets shut off mid-soak. Once everyone's clean and tucked in, the parents wind down and plan a sledding trip for the next day.

title: The Great Christmas Shopping Spree
synopsis: Morning coffee banter turns into an epic, increasingly absurd Christmas shopping trip: the parents debate telescopes, rocking chairs, and a mini tree before their gift list balloons past the 900th item. The spree spirals into daydreaming about a small fleet of new minivans, and maybe a Viper, just to haul all the presents home.

title: Toa Upgrades and a Fleet of Punch Buggies
synopsis: The shopping spree keeps escalating with talk of dangerous "Toa Nuva upgrade" kits and a debate over how many new cars, mostly punch buggies, the family actually needs. Back home, Grandma Pikachu cooks up her radish shish kebab and a spicy "super soup" for a hilariously crowded family dinner table full of hungry kids.

title: Invisible Wrapping on Christmas Eve
synopsis: On Christmas Eve, the family debates skipping the tree this year and unveils a goofy gift-wrapping trick, an "invisible" coating that hides the presents inside plain-looking boxes. Amid dish-cleaning and bath-time chores, someone poses the earnest question: does everyone actually know what Christmas is really about?

title: Tidying Up Before the Big Day
synopsis: A brief, low-key stretch of holiday tidying and quiet chatter, with a passing mention of getting a computer for Blossom as the kids help clear away the mess. Mostly light housekeeping talk with little narrated action.

title: Christmas Dinner, Dance, and the Sign-Off
synopsis: The family says grace, digs into the "famous soup," and closes out the night with an impromptu dance before cleaning up, though they note wistfully that the Toa never came home to get their Christmas present. The narrator formally wraps the sixth movie, jokes about his uncomfortable costume, and rattles off a list of camcorder effects and a mysterious 1999 side-project called "Doctor Senior 2000" before the tape drifts into chatter about an upcoming Pokemon-themed party with Crash, Coco, Spyro, and Meg.

title: Goldilocks and the Pee-Pee Dinner
synopsis: The kids act out a toy-and-Pokemon version of "Goldilocks and the Three Bears," complete with porridge, chairs, and beds, while also planning that night's dinner, jokingly dubbed the "pee-pee dinner" after a Pikachu gag. Everyone gets ready for guests, with Crash expected to be the first to arrive around 7:30.

title: Back After These Messages
synopsis: A goofy fake commercial break interrupts the action before returning to reheated pizza, Pikachu antics, and a running debate over what's appropriate for little Pikachu to watch on TV. Casual, low-key household chatter fills most of this stretch, with little else happening.

title: Pokemon Pancakes and Almost-Fireworks
synopsis: A scattered morning of silly mishaps: someone nearly blows a hole in the roof with a firework mix-up, breakfast turns into a running "Pokemon pancake" joke, and the household counts down to that evening's party, still set for 5:30.

title: Building a Snowmobile with Lego Pikachu
synopsis: Pikachu tinkers with a homemade snowmobile while the kids build Lego versions of Pikachu and an otter, plus a helicopter landing pad, in between a Pokemon-school day and hair-combing. The party countdown continues, now pegged at 5:45, as guests like Miss Coco start showing up.

title: Frosting, Vitamins, and a Half-Eaten Cake
synopsis: The party is in full swing: dishes get washed, treats get passed around, and the half-eaten cake gets topped with frosting and jelly for the kids. Amid the sugar rush there's a running gag about whether Pikachu got its vitamins, and someone brings up a mysterious "Fort Discovery."

title: The Puppy Cameo
synopsis: A brief, meandering wind-down after the party: more jelly jokes, a stray question about massage, and someone wondering what's next, before the camera catches a passing puppy and someone offers a cheerful hello to close things out.

title: Dr. Seinyor's Birthday Cake Caper
synopsis: The show opens with house rules from the cast before diving into chaos: Stacey whips up a birthday cake for Dr. Seinyor using suspiciously mixed 'potions' (really barbecue sauce and invisible milk) that turn into soup instead of pie. Meanwhile a frantic hotline call comes in warning that 'Ultimate Evil' -- the evil brother -- has returned for revenge, wielding the soul of Makuta. The gang scrambles to finish dinner and rush out to face him.

title: Enter the Toa Nuva and the Punch Buddies
synopsis: A special-report cutaway introduces the newest recruits to the Super Family: the six Toa Nuva, plus three Volkswagen New Beetles nicknamed the Punch Buddies -- Blackie, Barry, and Ruby. Battle resumes against the evil brother and Makuta, with heroes trading tail-and-head grabs, tennis-racket bombs, and boasts about unleashing their 'most powerful attacks.'

title: Tickles, Confusion, and Solar Beams
synopsis: The toy battle rolls on with a heavy dose of silliness -- a fighter gets reduced to giggles by a tickle attack before finally getting into position, while Pokemon-style moves like Confusion and Hyper get called out alongside a home-brewed 'solarize' beam meant to knock a foe out cold. Makuta gets accused of turning an enemy into a cartoon, and the narrator keeps interrupting to remind everyone about their forgotten most-powerful-attacks.

title: Cowboy Gear and the Cartoon Curse
synopsis: Combat gets weirder as one fighter suits up in cowboy gear for a 'wicked ride' while enemies keep getting hit with a move that turns them into literal, flickering cartoons. After trading taunts and a bazooka gag, the exhausted heroes declare the villains defeated and settle in to make camp for the night.

title: Shark Claw, Lightsabers, and Sheila's Accent
synopsis: A winged villain called Shark Claw squares off against the heroes, who counter with a lightsaber ('better than any old sword') and a mask of strength. A running bit has one character putting on a fake Australian accent as 'Sheila,' while the Powerpuff Girls make a surprise cameo, joining the fight with a taste-test gag before everyone unleashes their most powerful attacks.

title: The Rowdy Ruff Boys Crash the Fight
synopsis: The battle expands as the Rowdy Ruff Boys jump in against the heroes, trading boasts about being 'more powerful' than Makuta and the evil brother. A parade of goofy attack names -- Hyper Ray, Confusion, Beak Beam -- fly back and forth before the segment ends on a newcomer wielding a lightsaber.

title: Eagle Art Overload
synopsis: A dialogue-heavy but hard-to-follow stretch dominated by dozens of repeated 'Eagle Art' attack calls, tangled trash talk, and in-jokes about earlier Super Family movies. The transcript is unusually garbled here, but the gist is a chaotic multi-way battle building toward another most-powerful-attack showdown.

title: The One-on-One Chrono Duel
synopsis: Two fighters break off into a one-on-one battle, trading blows and boasts about their fencing training. Between rounds the kids bicker about a barrage of overly personal questions, and someone nurses a case of the hiccups after burning through two 'Chrono' power tokens in a row.

title: The Purple Chrono Swap
synopsis: Fighters burn through their Chrono resources one by one, squabbling over who gets the last swords and snacks. A running gag has Makuta ordering a favorite purple Chrono handed over against its owner's will, while a fire beam and a 'meanies must be destroyed' taunt round out the skirmish.

title: Super Pohatu Takes Flight
synopsis: One fighter discovers new claw weapons and declares himself 'Super Pohatu,' floating and scraping his way through a lighthearted scuffle full of poking, a soccer-ball head gag, and a rescued mask. The action winds down with the group resting after finally catching up to some 'big fat slowpokes.'

title: Pohatu's Gold Mask Gambit
synopsis: Pohatu digs up an old gold mask mid-battle and puts it back on for a fresh round of ground-beam attacks and underground ambush tactics. Lewa gets launched clean across the field, and the team debates whether to charge in or wait before regrouping.

title: Gally's Fire Staff and the Voice Box Caper
synopsis: Gally wields a fire staff while the group needles Makuta with a bit about swapping his voice box to make him 'sound like a girl.' Fighters cycle through pickety sticks, meditation breaks, and a running gag insisting that laughing is 'very good for your body,' before the mysterious XO Toa gets destroyed and the crew retreats to make pancakes.

title: Dr. Seinyor's Lightsaber Duel
synopsis: After a shish-kebab attack and a joke about Lewa being 'born four years ago on Christmas,' Dr. Seinyor announces he'll settle things with the evil brother in a personal lightsaber duel modeled on a Star Wars Jedi Power Battles clip, while the Toa Nuva handle Makuta. The evil brother bolts and leads Dr. Seinyor on a chase across hyper-jumps and an elevator before the Toa Nuva's fight resumes with Onua Nuva stepping up to battle.

title: Onua Nuva's New Arm Weapon
synopsis: The Toa Nuva fight continues as Onua Nuva steps up to battle, showing off a new arm weapon and mismatched leg gear before launching into hyper slashes and a soccer-style super kick. A sword duel follows, complete with a broken blade, repeated meditation breaks, and a running joke about strength and weakness being someone's 'temper.'

title: The Super Family's Final Stand
synopsis: The battle wraps up on the beach as the villain finally goes down for good, sputtering through a dramatic final-defeat speech before the credits roll. The episode closes out the movie with a teaser for the next Super Family video, promising it will be the longest one yet.

title: Stacey's Early Homecoming
synopsis: The eighth Super Family movie kicks off with house rules read by Amanda Young and opening credits naming Adam Young as director. The story follows Stacey coming home from college unexpectedly early, juggling phone calls, invisible bus fare, curtain-hiding from 'evil,' and looking after baby Sam and baby Jessica amid a peanut-butter mishap.

title: Silent Battle Stretch
synopsis: A mostly silent stretch of stop-motion battle action, with no narrated dialogue captured in this segment.

title: A Dropped Car and a Few Words
synopsis: Only a handful of stray lines were captured here -- a quick exchange about getting out of a chamber and dropping something -- inside what is otherwise a dialogue-light stretch of action.

title: The Quiet Battlefield
synopsis: A mostly silent stretch of stop-motion battle action, with no narrated dialogue captured in this segment.

title: Action Without Words
synopsis: A mostly silent stretch of stop-motion battle action, with no narrated dialogue captured in this segment.

title: A Silent Stretch of Battle
synopsis: A mostly silent stretch of stop-motion battle action, with no narrated dialogue captured in this segment.

title: Wordless Warfare
synopsis: A mostly silent stretch of stop-motion battle action, with no narrated dialogue captured in this segment.

title: Wavy Fingers and the Stinger Strike
synopsis: A quick burst of battle narration catches one fighter landing a devastating power move and a stinger strike so strong it stops the opponent cold. The narrator excitedly calls out immobilizing attacks and teases another fight still rolling on, before the recording cuts off mid-sentence. Short and scrappy, more toy-clash chaos than clear plot.

title: The Krona Switcheroo
synopsis: The heroes run desperately low on Krona, their spent power-masks, spitting them out and hoarding them, and even bluffing with an empty backup mask just in case Makuta's influence turns them again. A running gag interrupts the fight for a stern kids-don't-smoke PSA about a cigar-shaped mask piece. Loyalties blur into total confusion over who's evil now, until a booming voice cuts through the noise to remind everyone who the real enemy is.

title: Pea Brains and the Last Krona
synopsis: Makuta faces off again with no introductions needed this time, both sides scrambling to reload their very last Krona before the fight even starts. Between fireball charge-ups and a mask getting knocked clean off, the narrators bicker over whether "pea" is smart and whether a secret code might give the game away. It ends on a cliffhanger shout as Makuta declares himself very much alive.

title: Halftime with Stacy Senor
synopsis: The battle grinds on with masks and shields flying until the show abruptly cuts to a mock "Sports Center" halftime segment. A deadpan reporter interviews Stacy Senor about the ongoing eighth movie's battle, gets a shrug and a "good luck, make sure you win," then teases a "Stacy's Magical Moments" segment before technical difficulties send viewers off to find the ninth movie.

title: Crash, Coco, and the Bazooka Brigade
synopsis: Crash and Coco crash the battle as the annoying new arrivals, and the fight quickly turns into a chaotic arsenal showdown of Super Kicks, bazookas, and a howitzer or two. One combatant proudly reveals they've named their sixty-foot worm "Snakey," to everyone's disbelief, while another narrator daydreams of becoming the family's next Beam Master. Playful trash talk and misfired attacks carry the skirmish to its close.

title: Lunch Break and the Mimic Attack
synopsis: After a literal lunch-break interruption, the battle resumes with a dangerous copycat foe who mimics every attack thrown at her, countering Hyper Beams and Confusion moves right back at her attackers. The narrators dissolve into giggly chaos over dizziness, a "Shiny attack," and a bit where the villain declares herself the strongest of the whole gang before both sides claim to have failed.

title: The Crayon Thief's Fusion Trick
synopsis: A Fusion Attack and some very literal color-draining villainy take center stage, as one fighter threatens to suck all the color out of an opponent like a crayon. Amid rolly-polly jokes, a food-based aside, and a boast about a move called "Big Bashy Pringles Bash," the narrators keep tripping over each other's attack names as much as their toys trip over the battlefield. A tail catches fire just as the segment cuts off.

title: Evil Tigger's Secret Message
synopsis: Makuta sends an "Evil Piglet" and then an "Evil Tigger" to intercept a message, with Tigger cheerfully chanting "Happy day" while carrying out his dark orders. The narration wanders into real-life tangents about weekend plans and a Friday night show before snapping back to a squeeze-attack skirmish. It's a short, giggly stretch of toy-battle role-play more than plot.

title: The Voxor and the Exo-Tele
synopsis: A newly activated Voxor vehicle squares off against a rival fighter, with the narrators marveling at what an Exo-Tele could do by comparison. Masks get knocked loose and swapped between narrators mid-battle, and a countdown ticks toward a key return before the Voxor's power runs dry for the round.

title: Rendered Obsolete by the Exo-Toa
synopsis: A boastful Exo-Toa declares its abilities formidable enough to render its opponent's elemental powers obsolete, sparking an offended "why do you think I'm not a challenge" showdown. The narrators bring in a full lineup of challengers, including the Toa Nuva, before a vehicle rolls back in to needle everyone about who's really allowed to fight.

title: Snowball to the Face
synopsis: A long, sprawling battle stretch opens with someone getting smacked by a mock snowball and demanding a replacement mask after theirs flies clean across the field. Between weak-spot jokes, another "don't smoke, kids" cigar gag, and a wandering bit about a stolen arm, the wise Vakama steps in to call an opponent stupid before the vehicle chase resumes. It ends with a hunt for someone's missing tiny mask.

title: The Baloney Sandwich Standoff
synopsis: A telekinesis-and-vehicle skirmish gets derailed by a running joke about a "happy baloney sandwich" standing in for the looming Universal War. A masked servant of Makuta threatens to slash a rival to bits, but the fight dissolves into a search for a lost mask and its spirit, last seen blown off in the chaos.

title: Prophecy 26 and the Exotope
synopsis: A newly summoned Exotope creature enters the fray as the narrators debate weak spots, electric powers, and how to properly aim a "Raptor Rocket" at its mask. Bait, borrowed swords, and a swapped-out red mask keep the skirmish moving, capped by a silly threat to jam a sword down a rival's throat -- both of them.

title: Berries, Beans, and Super Confusion
synopsis: A trap springs and a barrage of watermelon and berry gags sends the battle into a giddy "charge up" frenzy, complete with a rapid-fire Confusion and Super Confusion exchange. One fighter starts pinning captured strength-masks to their own hand to steal their power, boasting "I have super strength!" as the skirmish winds down toward a near-knockout.

title: Prophecy 27 and the Gold Masks
synopsis: Talk turns to rare gold masks and a mysterious, more powerful ally as the narrators invoke a prophecy and its promised champion. A running bit about "mocking" versus making fun -- capped by a deadpan "what's two plus two? four" -- needles the villain, while masks and shields get knocked loose across a long, back-and-forth exchange.

title: The Koly Ball Kick-Off
synopsis: Between talk of surfing and a homemade "pizza monster," one fighter shows off turning their grabber claws into a fast-rolling koly ball for the fight. Masks pile up as trophies, kicks fly at varying strength "for the kids," and the segment closes on a chant of "I think I can" before the villain concedes defeat.

title: Don't Mistreat an Oyster
synopsis: Between armor swaps and a running joke about a mask that makes its wearer look noseless, the narrators debate the merits of gold masks supposedly coming soon to a mask shop. A mid-battle detour has one narrator literally rummaging through an attic for a sound effect, and the segment wraps with an oddly specific PSA: don't try this at home, and definitely don't mistreat an oyster.

title: Waka's Walnut Brain
synopsis: Makuta shows up looking different this time, now with a flying creature attached to his thigh and a pair of not-actually-tickling guns, as the narrators trade jabs about hollow heads and a rival's walnut-sized brain. A pesky flying bug briefly steals the spotlight before the fight's last attack gets teased and the segment cuts over to Stacy.

title: The Spirit of Destruction Revealed
synopsis: Dr. Seinyor faces down Makuta's true form, who reveals himself as the very Krana in front of them -- the self-proclaimed "spirit of destruction." A tense, surprisingly philosophical exchange follows about why destroying him would be self-defeating, needing only chaos, destruction, and war to win, before Dr. Seinyor claims special training and the battle finally begins.

title: Fighter Mode, Walking Mode
synopsis: The climactic showdown with Makuta escalates as the villain vows to escape and return within a year to unleash the Universal War if not destroyed now. Dr. Seinyor closes in for the finishing blow while a creature is sent in to "suck his soul out," and the fight cycles through dramatic mode-switches -- fighter mode, walking mode -- as a transformation begins.

title: Pay for What You've Done
synopsis: The final confrontation between Dr. Seinyor and Makuta replays and escalates, with the villain again threatening a year in hiding and a Universal War if he survives. A monstrous ally moves in to finish him off as the narrators call out "fighter mode" and "walking mode" over dramatic sound effects, ending on Makuta's defiant demand: "pay for what you've done to me."

title: See You at the AC
synopsis: In a brief closing beat, Makuta concedes total defeat -- "the Super Family has defeated me" -- and skulks off with a threat to return. The narrator signs off teasing the tenth movie and a coming war, promising to see everyone at the AC.
